The screening exercise, coordinated by the Federation of Oyo State Students’ Union (FOSSU) National, is currently underway for eligible students in universities, polytechnics, colleges of education and other specialised institutions across the country. Speaking during the ongoing screening exercise at the Oyo State Ministry of Education, Science and Technology, the 10th Senate President of FOSSU, Distinguished Senator Yekinni Sodiq, said the bursary programme reflects Governor Makinde’s commitment to supporting students and easing the financial burden associated with higher education. According to him, a total of 5,000 final-year students across the country successfully registered for the scheme. Sodiq explained that the programme was open to final-year students of Oyo State origin studying at accredited tertiary institutions, provided they met the stipulated requirements. He urged beneficiaries to make judicious use of the funds, noting that the bursary would not only support their academic pursuits but also assist students engaged in small-scale businesses and other productive ventures. Also speaking, the Head of Government to the FOSSU National President, Hon. Kamil-Bello Umar-Farouk, commended Governor Makinde for sustaining the bursary scheme since assuming office and for continually expanding opportunities for Oyo State students. Farouk disclosed that students enrolled in Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE) programmes who were excluded from the previous edition of the scheme have now been included following appeals to the Governor. “Last year, NCE students were not captured under the bursary scheme. We appealed to the Governor because they are also stakeholders in the education sector and deserving beneficiaries. We are grateful that His Excellency approved their inclusion this year, and they will now benefit from the programme,” he said. He revealed that Makinde approved an increase in the bursary awards in response to requests from student representatives. According to him, while beneficiaries received a flat bursary of N100,000 in the previous edition, the revised structure now provides enhanced support across student categories. “NCE students will receive N100,000 each, while polytechnic students will receive N150,000. Students at universities and other tertiary institutions will each receive N200,000. Medical and clinical students, law graduates in Law School, as well as aviation students, will receive N500,000 each,” Farouk stated. He described the increase as another demonstration of the governor’s responsiveness to students’ welfare and educational advancement in the state. Farouk also appreciated the Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Student Affairs, Hon. Victor Olojede, for his efforts toward the successful implementation of the programme. He equally commended the FOSSU leadership for its commitment to advancing the interests of Oyo State students. “On behalf of Oyo State students across Nigeria and beyond, we express our profound appreciation to Governor Seyi Makinde for this intervention. We remain grateful for his unwavering commitment to the welfare and educational development of students in the state,” he added. The bursary scheme forms part of the Makinde administration’s broader efforts to promote access to education, encourage academic excellence, and reduce the financial challenges students face as they complete their studies.
